The PR adds workspace profile administration, ownership transfer and deletion, persistent icons, durable upload cleanup, settings UI wiring, and a Windows-safe SDK build helper.

Reproducibility: yes. for the introduced transfer-selection defect: create more than 200 eligible human members and attempt to select a target outside the first page; source inspection shows that no subsequent cursor is requested. Reproduction is otherwise not applicable to the feature request itself.

target.title: fix(cli,doctor): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

CLI capability and doctor migration code uses `"apiKey" in <configObj>` and bracket-keyed `<obj>[providerId]` lookups to check whether credential ApiKey fields and provider-map entries are present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property (e.g. via `Object.create({apiKey: "injected"})`) could be mistaken for an explicit user credential entry or a configured provider.

This is **defensive runtime-object hardening** — the raw POJO config from `JSON.parse()` is plain, but runtime intermediate objects (results of `resolveTtsConfig`, `resolveLegacySearchConfig`, etc.) are assembled from multiple sources. Using `in`/bracket access on these objects means inherited `__proto__` properties survive until the `Object.hasOwn()` gate. Switching to `Object.hasOwn()` hardens these internal runtime objects so inherited properties are never mistaken for explicit user config.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. All config-like objects are plain POJOs or `Object.create(null)` runtime records, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while hardening the runtime boundary. Every bracket-keyed provider lookup (`obj[providerId]`) is also guarded with `Object.hasOwn()` before accessing the dynamic key.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as explicit credential entries or configured providers in:
- TTS provider config API key detection (`ttsProviderConfigHasApiKey`)
- TTS resolved provider config lookup (`resolvedTtsConfigHasProviderApiKey`)
- Legacy web-search migration entry detection match + fix (`listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths`, `hasMappedLegacyWebSearchConfig`, `copyLegacyProviderConfig`)

### Evidence

**Redacted after-fix CLI reproduction** — exercises the real doctor migration module (`listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths` + `migrateLegacyWebSearchConfig`) against three config scenarios:

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  Redacted doctor reproduction — after fix                    ║
║  Module: listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths + migrateLegacyWeb-  ║
║          SearchConfig (doctor --fix --config-only)           ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

── Config A (legitimate own entries) ──
  Doctor match phase: listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths
    → 4 path(s): ["tools.web.search.apiKey","tools.web.search.grok.apiKey",
                   "tools.web.search.grok.model","tools.web.search.kimi.apiKey"]
  Doctor fix phase: migrateLegacyWebSearchConfig
    → 3 migration(s):
       • Moved tools.web.search.apiKey → plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey.
       • Moved tools.web.search.grok → plugins.entries.xai.config.webSearch.
       • Moved tools.web.search.kimi → plugins.entries.moonshot.config.webSearch.

── Config B (all proto-inherited) ──
  Doctor match phase: listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths
    → 0 paths → doctor config check skipped (no false match ✅)
  Doctor fix phase: migrateLegacyWebSearchConfig
    → 0 migrations (no spurious entries ✅)

── Config C (own apiKey + proto provider) ──
  Doctor match phase: listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths
    → 1 path(s): ["tools.web.search.apiKey"]
  Doctor fix phase: migrateLegacyWebSearchConfig
    → 1 migration(s):
       • Moved tools.web.search.apiKey → plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey.

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  Summary                                                     ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  Legitimate (own)      4        3          ✓ backward compat ║
║  Proto-forged (all)    0        0          ✓ skipped         ║
║  Mixed (own+proto)     1        1          ✓ own only        ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

**Unit tests** — regression cases inlined into existing caller-level suites, helpers kept private:
```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  120 passed (120)
        └── src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.test.ts — 10 (6 existing + 4 own-property)
        └── src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts — 110 (109 existing + 1 proto-inherited guard integration test)
```

### Replacements

| File | Function | Guard change |
|------|----------|-------------|
| `src/cli/capability-cli.ts` | `ttsProviderConfigHasApiKey` | `"apiKey" in value` → `Object.hasOwn(value, "apiKey")` |
| `src/cli/capability-cli.ts` | `resolvedTtsConfigHasProviderApiKey` | `config.providerConfigs[providerId]` → `Object.hasOwn(config.providerConfigs, providerId) && …` |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths` | `"apiKey" in search` → `Object.hasOwn(search, "apiKey")` |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths` | `search[providerId]` → `Object.hasOwn(search, providerId) ? … : undefined` |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `hasMappedLegacyWebSearchConfig` | `isRecord(search[providerId])` → `Object.hasOwn(search, providerId) && isRecord(…)` |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `copyLegacyProviderConfig` | `search[providerKey]` → `Object.hasOwn(search, providerKey) ? … : undefined` |
